title: Istruzione, scienza e tecnologia
sub: Word formation, collocazioni e connettivi - discussione accademica e saggio B2 First
grammar: Word formation (prefissi e suffissi), collocazioni, connettivi (although, despite, whereas, nevertheless)

lessons.title: Word formation, collocazioni e connettivi
lessons.intro: L'ultima unità del corso mette insieme tre strumenti che il B2 First chiede in ogni parte: formare parole con prefissi e suffissi, scegliere le collocazioni giuste e collegare le idee con i connettivi di contrasto (although, despite, whereas, nevertheless).

steps.title: Word formation: suffissi
steps.body:
Da una parola-radice si ottengono nomi, aggettivi, verbi e avverbi con i **suffissi**. Prima di scrivere chiediti sempre **che parte del discorso serve** nella frase.
- **Nomi**: -tion / -sion (decide -> decision), -ment (achieve -> achievement), -ness (kind -> kindness), -ity (able -> ability), -ence / -ance (depend -> dependence), -ship (friend -> friendship), -ism (critic -> criticism); persone: -er / -or / -ist / -ian.
- **Aggettivi**: -able / -ible (rely -> reliable), -ful (success -> successful), -less (care -> careless), -ous (danger -> dangerous), -ive (create -> creative), -al (culture -> cultural), -ic (history -> historic).
- **Verbi**: -ise / -ize (modern -> modernise), -en (wide -> widen), -ify (simple -> simplify).
- **Avverbi**: -ly (careful -> carefully; happy -> happily).

Attenzione ai cambiamenti di ortografia: la -y diventa -i (happy -> happiness), la -e finale cade (create -> creation), a volte cambia la radice (succeed -> success, decide -> decision). E controlla se il nome deve essere plurale: one achievement / many achievements.
ex: Her determination was impressive.
La sua determinazione era impressionante.
The decision was made without any discussion.
La decisione è stata presa senza alcuna discussione.

steps.title: Word formation: prefissi
steps.body:
I **prefissi** cambiano il significato, spesso in negativo, ma non la parte del discorso.
- **Negativi**: un- (happy -> unhappy), in- (visible -> invisible), dis- (agree -> disagree), non- (existent -> non-existent), mis- (understand -> misunderstand, «sbagliare»).
- **in- diventa**: **im-** prima di b, m, p (impossible, immature); **il-** prima di l (illegal); **ir-** prima di r (irregular, irresponsible).
- **Altri prefissi**: over- (overworked: troppo), under- (underpaid), re- (rewrite: di nuovo), out- (outgrow: superare), pre- (preview), inter- (international), ex- (ex-president).

Nel tuo ragionamento: se la frase suona negativa («She was ___ to find a job»), probabilmente serve un prefisso negativo. Ma non tutte le radici accettano tutti i prefissi: si dice **unable, impossible, disagree, dishonest**, mai «inable» o «unpossible». Se ti sembra una parola italiana, controllala: in inglese si dice **unemployment** (non «disoccupation»).
ex: It is impossible to predict the weather exactly.
È impossibile prevedere esattamente il tempo.
She felt underpaid and overworked.
Si sentiva sottopagata e sovraccarica di lavoro.

steps.title: Collocazioni e make / do
steps.body:
Le **collocazioni** sono coppie di parole che «stanno bene insieme» e non si possono tradurre parola per parola. Le più frequenti ai test:
- **do**: research, homework, a course, damage, harm, your best, a favour.
- **make**: progress, a decision, a mistake, an effort, an attempt, a suggestion, a complaint, an impression.
- **carry out / conduct**: an experiment, a survey, research (formale).
- **draw / reach**: a conclusion. **meet**: a deadline, requirements. **take**: part, advantage, notice. **pay**: attention, a visit.
- Aggettivi: **heavy** rain / traffic / smoker; **strong** wind / coffee / evidence; **bitter** disappointment; **deeply** concerned; **highly** unlikely.

**Errori tipici degli italiani**: «do a mistake», «make research», «make progresses» (progress non è numerabile), «take a decision» (in UK si dice **make a decision**). Impara le collocazioni in blocco, con il verbo.
ex: She did a lot of research for her thesis.
Ha fatto molte ricerche per la tesi.
We made good progress today.
Oggi abbiamo fatto buoni progressi.
The team carried out an experiment.
Il gruppo ha condotto un esperimento.

steps.title: Connettivi: contrasto, addizione, conseguenza
steps.body:
I connettivi collegano le idee e sono decisivi nel saggio. Attenzione alla **costruzione che li segue**:
- **Although / even though / though + frase**: Although it was late, we kept working. (non «although... but»)
- **Despite / in spite of + nome o -ing**: Despite the rain... / In spite of being tired... (non «despite of»). Con una frase: despite **the fact that** he was tired.
- **Whereas / while + frase**: contrasto tra due cose: Tom loves maths, whereas his sister prefers languages.
- **However / nevertheless / nonetheless**: all'inizio di una frase, con virgola: The test was hard. Nevertheless, most students passed.
- **Addizione**: moreover, furthermore, in addition (to + nome / -ing).
- **Conseguenza**: therefore, consequently, as a result. **Scopo**: in order to / so that.
- **Condizione**: provided (that), as long as, unless.

**Errori tipici degli italiani**: «Despite of the weather», «Although he was ill, but he went», «Despite he was ill» (serve the fact that).
table: Although he was ill, he came.
I like tea, whereas he likes coffee.
He was ill. Nevertheless, he came.
ex: Although she was tired, she kept studying.
Sebbene fosse stanca, continuò a studiare.
Despite the cost, the course was worth it.
Nonostante il costo, il corso valeva la pena.
Some prefer lectures, whereas others learn alone.
Alcuni preferiscono le lezioni, mentre altri imparano da soli.

steps.s: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
steps.why: Dopo although segue una frase completa (soggetto + verbo).

steps.s: ___ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
steps.why: Despite è seguito da un nome: the heavy traffic.

steps.s: Some students prefer lectures, ___ others learn better in small groups.
steps.why: Whereas collega due cose in contrasto.

steps.s: The experiment failed. ___, the team did not give up.
steps.why: Nevertheless introduce un contrasto con la frase precedente.

opts: Despite the rain, we enjoyed the trip.
Despite of the rain, we enjoyed the trip.
Despite it rained, we enjoyed the trip.
steps.why: Despite non vuole of e non regge una frase: serve un nome o -ing.

steps.q: I have to ___ some research before I start writing my essay.
steps.why: La collocazione è do research.

steps.q: Completa con una o più parole

answers: Despite
In spite of

lessons.title: Istruzione, scienza e tecnologia
lessons.intro: Il lessico di università, ricerca e tecnologia: serve per le letture dell'esame, per i saggi su scuola e innovazione e per le discussioni accademiche.

ex: She won a scholarship to study engineering in Edinburgh.
Ha vinto una borsa di studio per studiare ingegneria a Edimburgo.
Plagiarism can lead to a student being expelled.
Il plagio può portare all'espulsione di uno studente.
He is writing his dissertation on renewable energy.
Sta scrivendo la tesi sulle energie rinnovabili.
words.note: Per la tesi di dottorato si usa di solito thesis.

ex: Scientists announced a breakthrough in cancer research.
Gli scienziati hanno annunciato una svolta nella ricerca sul cancro.
words.note: Si dice a breakthrough in + campo.

ex: The laboratory uses cutting-edge technology.
Il laboratorio usa tecnologia all'avanguardia.
The algorithm recommends videos based on what you watch.
L'algoritmo consiglia video in base a quello che guardi.
Many students drop out during their first year.
Molti studenti abbandonano gli studi durante il primo anno.
words.note: Drop out of university / school. Il nome è a dropout.

ex: It is hard to keep up with new technology.
È difficile tenere il passo con le nuove tecnologie.
Distance learning allows people to study while working.
La formazione a distanza permette di studiare lavorando.
Our lecturer gives very clear explanations.
Il nostro docente dà spiegazioni molto chiare.
Coding is now part of the school curriculum.
Programmare ora fa parte del programma scolastico.
words.note: Plurale: curricula. Il CV si dice CV o résumé, non «curriculum».

ex: Digital literacy is as important as reading and writing.
Le competenze digitali sono importanti quanto leggere e scrivere.
Automation has replaced thousands of factory jobs.
L'automazione ha sostituito migliaia di posti di lavoro in fabbrica.
Teenagers are strongly influenced by their peers.
Gli adolescenti sono fortemente influenzati dai coetanei.

steps.why: Keep up with = tenere il passo con.

steps.why: Una borsa di studio paga le spese: scholarship.

answers: plagiarism

opts: Una scoperta o un progresso importante

lessons.title: Imparare con le macchine
lessons.intro: Un articolo sull'intelligenza artificiale a scuola, con voci a favore e contro. È un testo da B2 First: argomentazione, connettivi di contrasto e vocabolario di istruzione e tecnologia.

steps.title: Can a machine teach?
steps.text:
Ten years ago, a classroom without a blackboard would have seemed strange. Today, in many schools, the blackboard has been replaced by a tablet, and the teacher's red pen by software that corrects homework in seconds. Supporters of educational technology argue that this is not a gimmick but a revolution. Critics reply that we are rushing into something we do not fully understand.

Consider the case of Wexford Academy, a secondary school in the north of England that introduced an artificial intelligence tutor two years ago. Each pupil receives exercises adapted to their level: a student who struggles with fractions is offered more practice, whereas one who has mastered them moves on to harder problems. According to the head teacher, maths results have improved by almost fifteen per cent. Teachers, who once spent their evenings marking, now have more time to talk to individual pupils. "The software does the repetitive work," she says, "so we can do the human work."

Nevertheless, not everyone is convinced. Dr Helen Marsh, a researcher in education, points out that most studies have been short and carried out by the companies that sell the products. "Although the early results look encouraging, we simply do not have enough independent evidence," she says. She also worries about privacy. Every answer a pupil types is recorded, and nobody can say with certainty where that data will end up in ten years' time.

Another concern is plagiarism and dependence. Since chatbots can write a passable essay in a few seconds, some teachers have returned to handwritten exams, while others have gone in the opposite direction and encourage pupils to use the tools openly, provided that they explain how. Neither approach is perfect. Banning technology is difficult to enforce, and allowing it without limits risks producing students who can never think for themselves.

Perhaps the most balanced view comes from a teacher at the school, Mr Okafor. Despite being enthusiastic about the new tools, he insists that they should remain assistants, not replacements. "A machine can tell a child that an answer is wrong," he says, "but it cannot notice that she is upset, or that she is afraid to ask a question." Learning, he argues, is not just the transfer of information; it is a relationship.

If he is right, the real challenge is not whether schools should use technology, but how. The most successful classrooms, researchers suggest, are those where teachers decide when a tool is useful and when it is not. Technology, in other words, is a very good servant but a poor master, and the sooner schools and parents understand this, the better the results are likely to be.

opts: He presents the views of both supporters and critics.
He explains how a tablet works.
qs.why: Prima i sostenitori («a revolution»), poi i critici («rushing into something»).

opts: It gives extra practice to those who struggle and moves others on.
It sets the same work for everyone.
It marks only the best pupils.
qs.why: «a student who struggles with fractions is offered more practice, whereas one who has mastered them moves on».

opts: They have more time to talk to individual pupils.
qs.why: «now have more time to talk to individual pupils».

qs.q: Why is Dr Marsh cautious about the early results?
opts: Most studies were short and run by the companies selling the products.
qs.why: «most studies have been short and carried out by the companies that sell the products».

opts: Nobody knows where pupils' data will end up in the future.
qs.why: «nobody can say with certainty where that data will end up in ten years' time».

qs.q: How have schools reacted to essay-writing chatbots?
opts: All of them have banned them.
All of them allow them freely.
In different ways: some ban them, others allow them with conditions.
qs.why: «some teachers have returned to handwritten exams, while others... encourage pupils to use the tools openly».

qs.q: What is Mr Okafor's opinion about the new tools?
opts: They should remain assistants, not replacements.

answers: master
qs.why: «a very good servant but a poor master».

steps.why: Gimmick = trovata, trucco per fare effetto.
Passable = sufficiente, che può passare.

steps.s: Banning technology is difficult ___ .
steps.why: Difficult + to + infinito: to enforce.

answers: provided
providing
steps.why: Provided (that) = a condizione che.

lessons.title: Un colloquio con il tutor
lessons.intro: Una studentessa discute la sua tesi con il relatore. Ascolta come chiede chiarimenti e quali consigli riceve su metodo, campione e scadenze.

steps.title: A dissertation tutorial
steps.it: Ascolta il colloquio. Puoi riascoltarlo e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Come in, Aisha. Take a seat. So, how is the dissertation going?
Well, I've finished the literature review, but I'm having trouble with the methodology. I'm not sure whether I should use interviews or a questionnaire.
What exactly is your research question?
I want to find out whether students who study online perform as well as those who attend lectures.
I see. In that case, a questionnaire alone probably won't be enough. You would get opinions, but not evidence of performance. Have you considered comparing exam results as well?
Sorry, could you explain what you mean by comparing? Do you mean using the university's data?
Yes, exactly. You'd need permission from the department, and the data would have to be anonymous. That can take a few weeks, so I'd apply straight away.
Right. And what about the sample size? I was planning to ask around forty students.
That's a bit small. Ideally you'd want eighty or more, otherwise your results won't be reliable. Although a smaller study can still be useful if you're clear about its limitations.
Could I just check something? Does that mean I should include a section on limitations?
Definitely. Examiners like students who recognise the weaknesses of their own work, whereas weak dissertations pretend that everything is perfect.
Thank you, that's very helpful. When would you like to see the next draft?
Let's say the fifteenth of March. That gives you six weeks. Email it to me beforehand, and we'll meet on the Friday.
Perfect. I'll make a start this afternoon.
Good. And remember, don't leave the references until the last minute. Every year, somebody loses marks for sloppy referencing, and it is such a waste of good work.
Understood. I'll start a reference list today and keep it up to date as I write.

qs.q: What is Aisha having trouble with?
What does her research want to find out?
opts: Whether online students perform as well as those who attend lectures
qs.why: «whether students who study online perform as well as those who attend lectures».

qs.q: Why is a questionnaire alone not enough?
opts: It shows opinions, not evidence of performance.
The university does not allow it.
qs.why: «You would get opinions, but not evidence of performance».

qs.q: Before using the exam data, Aisha must get ___ from the department.
answers: permission

qs.q: How many students does Dr Reid recommend?
Why should Aisha include a section on limitations?
opts: Examiners like students who recognise the weaknesses of their work.
qs.why: «Examiners like students who recognise the weaknesses of their own work».

qs.q: When is the next draft due?
opts: On the Friday of next week

steps.en: Sorry, could you explain what you mean by comparing?
steps.it: Scusi, potrebbe spiegare che cosa intende per confrontare?

steps.en: Examiners like students who recognise the weaknesses of their own work.
steps.it: Agli esaminatori piacciono gli studenti che riconoscono i punti deboli del proprio lavoro.

lessons.title: Discussione accademica
lessons.intro: Come si chiedono chiarimenti, si riformula quanto detto e si presentano risultati con prudenza in un seminario o durante un colloquio con il docente.

steps.title: Chiedere chiarimenti e riformulare
steps.body:
In un contesto accademico è normale chiedere di spiegare meglio:
- **Could you clarify what you mean by...?** = Potrebbe chiarire che cosa intende con...?
- **I'm not sure I follow.** = Non sono sicuro di seguire.
- **Could you give an example?** = Potrebbe fare un esempio?
- **Could you go over that again, please?** = Potrebbe ripetere?
- **Do you mean that...?** / **So what you're saying is...** = Vuole dire che... / Quindi sta dicendo che...
- **If I understand correctly, ...** = Se ho capito bene...

Per riformulare una tua frase: **Let me put it another way.** / **What I mean is...**
**Errore tipico degli italiani**: «Can you explain me?». In inglese: **explain something to someone** (Could you explain it to me?).
ex: Could you clarify what you mean by sample size?
Potrebbe chiarire che cosa intende con dimensione del campione?
If I understand correctly, the results are not reliable.
Se ho capito bene, i risultati non sono affidabili.

steps.title: Presentare risultati con prudenza
steps.body:
Nei testi e nei discorsi accademici si evita di dire cose troppo assolute. Si usano formule di cautela:
- **It seems that... / It appears that...**
- **This may suggest that... / The results suggest that...**
- **tends to**, **in most cases**, **to some extent**
- **One limitation of the study is that...**
- **Further research is needed.**

Per indicare un risultato: **The main finding was that...** / **According to the data...** / **This shows that...** (più deciso). Evita «This proves that...», che di solito è troppo forte.
ex: The results suggest that online learners perform as well as others.
I risultati suggeriscono che chi studia online rende quanto gli altri.
One limitation is the small sample.
Un limite è il campione ridotto.

steps.title: In a seminar
steps.it: Scegli la battuta più adatta a un contesto accademico.
lines: So the study found a strong correlation between sleep and exam results, but this does not prove a cause.

opts: Sorry, could you clarify the difference between correlation and cause?
I don't understand anything, explain me.

lines: A correlation means two things happen together. A cause means one produces the other.

opts: I see. Could you give an example?

lines: Of course. Ice cream sales and sunburn rise together, but ice cream does not cause sunburn.

opts: If I understand correctly, something else, like hot weather, causes both.
So the ice cream is dangerous.
I'm not agree, ice cream is good.

steps.why: Le formule Could you clarify, Could you give an example e If I understand correctly mostrano interesse e rendono la conversazione precisa.

It's all wrong, I can't do it.
I don't know, you are the tutor.

Yes, I know what a topic sentence is.
I don't have time for this.

pairs: Could you clarify what you mean?

alts: The results are not reliable if I understand correctly

steps.it: Potrebbe chiarire che cosa intende con questo?

steps.en: I'm not sure I follow. Could you give an example?

steps.q: You are in a seminar and the lecturer has just explained a new idea. Ask for clarification, summarise what you understood and mention one possible weakness.
steps.it: Sei a un seminario: chiedi un chiarimento, riassumi quello che hai capito e indica un possibile punto debole (almeno 5 frasi).
steps.model: Sorry, could you clarify what you mean by sustainable growth? If I understand correctly, it means growing the economy without damaging the environment. So what you're saying is that both goals can be achieved together. I find that interesting, but one limitation might be that it depends on new technology, which is still expensive. Could you give an example of a country where this has worked?

lessons.title: Il saggio B2 First
lessons.intro: Il saggio completo del B2 First: due punti dati dalla traccia più una tua idea. Struttura, registro, connettivi e lingua sono quelli che valuta l'esaminatore. Poi due attività di parlato.

steps.title: Il saggio B2 First (Part 1)
steps.body:
Nella Part 1 della prova di scrittura ricevi un tema e **due punti** da trattare; devi aggiungere **una tua idea** (own idea). Devi scrivere 140-190 parole in registro neutro-formale.

Struttura consigliata:
- **Introduzione**: presenta il tema e la tua posizione.
- **Punto 1** (primo paragrafo): argomento con spiegazione e, se puoi, esempio.
- **Punto 2**: lo stesso, possibilmente con un contrasto.
- **La tua idea**: un terzo punto originale, introdotto da In my opinion / Another factor is...
- **Conclusione**: To sum up, I believe... (senza nuove idee).

**Connettivi** che danno punteggio: although, despite, whereas, nevertheless, moreover, as a result, in order to. **Lingua**: varia le strutture: un passivo, un condizionale, una frase scissa o un'inversione. **Collocazioni** precise: make a decision, carry out research, raise awareness.
Niente contrazioni e niente linguaggio colloquiale; non copiare le parole della traccia e controlla di aver trattato tutti i punti.
ex: The first issue is cost.
Il primo problema è il costo.
To sum up, a balanced approach is best.
In sintesi, un approccio equilibrato è il migliore.

steps.q: Quale connettivo introduce correttamente un contrasto con la frase precedente?
steps.why: Dopo una difficoltà serve un contrasto: Nevertheless.

steps.q: In your English class you have been talking about technology in schools. Your teacher has asked you to write an essay. Write an essay using all the notes and give reasons for your point of view. Should schools replace textbooks with tablets? Notes: Write about: 1. cost 2. concentration 3. (your own idea)
steps.it: Scrivi il saggio (140-190 parole): tratta il costo, la concentrazione e una tua idea personale, motivando la tua opinione. Usa almeno tre connettivi di contrasto o addizione.
checklist: Contenuto: ho trattato i due punti e aggiunto una mia idea, con una chiara opinione
Organizzazione: introduzione, un paragrafo per punto, conclusione, con connettivi
Lingua: ho usato almeno tre connettivi (although, despite, whereas, nevertheless...) e collocazioni precise
Ho rispettato il numero di parole (140-190)
useful: In my opinion, there is another factor: ...
To sum up, I believe that...
steps.model:
Nowadays, many schools are replacing textbooks with tablets. Although this change has clear advantages, it also raises some important questions.

The first issue is cost. Tablets are expensive, and they need to be repaired or replaced more often than books. However, once schools have bought them, they can save money on printing, since digital books are usually cheaper and can be updated at no cost.

The second point is concentration. Whereas a textbook contains only the lesson, a tablet also offers games and messages, so pupils may be easily distracted. Nevertheless, with clear rules and the right software, teachers can limit this problem.

In my opinion, there is a third factor: health. Spending hours in front of a screen can harm children's eyesight and posture, so paper still has a role to play.

To sum up, I believe that tablets should be used alongside textbooks, rather than instead of them. Despite the benefits of technology, a balanced approach is the best way to protect both learning and well-being.

steps.q: Do you think smartphones should be banned in schools? Give reasons.
steps.it: Dì se secondo te gli smartphone andrebbero vietati a scuola e perché (almeno 5 frasi).
steps.model: In my opinion, smartphones should be restricted but not completely banned. Although they can distract pupils, they are also useful for research and for emergencies. On the other hand, children who spend the whole lesson looking at a screen learn very little. Therefore, I think teachers should decide when phones can be used. To sum up, clear rules are better than a total ban.

steps.q: Describe a piece of technology that has changed the way you study or work.
steps.it: Descrivi una tecnologia che ha cambiato il tuo modo di studiare o lavorare (almeno 5 frasi).
hints: Before I had it, I used to...
steps.model: The piece of technology that has changed my work most is my laptop. It allows me to work from anywhere and to keep all my documents in one place. Before I had it, I used to carry heavy folders everywhere. However, one disadvantage is that I find it harder to switch off in the evening. Even so, I could not imagine working without it.
